newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says global telecoms deal will reduce costs.
newsitem.headline: Japan says global telecoms deal will reduce costs.

text.p: Japan's Posts and Telecommunications Minister Hisao Horinouchi said a global telecoms agreement reached over the weekend would help reduce costs and offer a wider range of services to customers.
Sixty-eight countries, including the United States and Japan, agreed in Geneva on Saturday to open up most of the world's $600 billion telecommunications market.
"I am extremely pleased that the WTO (World Trade Organisation) Negotiations on Basic Telecommunications were brought to a successful conclusion," Horinouchi said in statement on Sunday.
"The success of the negotiations in introducing liberalisation and competition to the field of telecommunications will enable rates to be reduced and services to be diversified," Horinouchi said.
"In addition, the new agreement marks the beginning of a new era which promises the realisation of a global information infrastructure," he said.

Japan offered to lift all of its restrictions on foreign ownership of telecommunications operators, including wireless businesses, except for industry giants Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) and Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co (KDD), which will retain a 20 percent foreign ownership limit.
